discoveries.title: Legora Raises $550M at $5.55B Valuation in Landmark Legal AI Funding Round
discoveries.summary: <cite index="4-30,4-31">On March 10, Stockholm-based Legora announced a $550 million Series D led by Accel, with participation from Benchmark, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Iconiq, Redpoint Ventures, and Y Combinator. The round valued the company at $5.55 billion -- tripling its valuation from an October 2025 round just five months earlier.</cite> The funding wave comes alongside Harvey's $200M raise, creating combined $16 billion in legal AI enterprise value.

discoveries.title: SRA Authorizes Second Technology-Only Law Firm with Non-AI Deterministic System
discoveries.summary: <cite index="18-24,18-25">A technology-only law firm built around a "fully deterministic legal model" has been authorised by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), the first of its kind. LawFairy's system encodes the law into structured decision pathways to reach an auditable output, in contrast to generative AI, which generates responses by predicting statistically likely text.</cite> This follows Garfield AI as the second SRA-authorized tech-only firm, but explicitly avoids AI in favor of rule-based systems.

discoveries.title: Law Society of Scotland Makes AI in Legal Sector Key Project for 2026
discoveries.summary: <cite index="13-12">The Society has made AI in the legal sector a key project for 2026.</cite> The project comes alongside new guidance warning that <cite index="13-20,13-21">the regulatory framework has not yet taken AI's presence into account. Current regulation is principles-based, requiring compliance with existing professional standards.</cite> This represents a major regulatory development for Scottish legal practice.

discoveries.title: USCIS Deploys PAiTH Internal AI Assistant for Immigration Processing
discoveries.summary: <cite index="49-9,49-10,49-11">PAiTH (Private AI Tech Hub) will serve as USCIS's internal AI workforce assistant, deployed in the USCIS Private Cloud development zero environment. The system will provide role-specific AI assistance to USCIS staff across six functional areas: contracts/acquisition, legal research, language translation, software development, security compliance, and financial operations. PAiTH will enable USCIS employees to interact with an AI assistant tailored to their job function.</cite> This represents significant government adoption of AI in immigration processing.
